item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-4e80e59c6cb9cbc8","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"On 3 March 2023, Tshisekedi instructed ministries, security services, the CENI, courts, and tribunals to protect electoral materials and voters, pursue and severely punish theft, destruction, falsification, violence, stigmatization, exclusion, and discrimination, and report regularly on electoral-security procedures. The CENI reported more than 25 million voters enrolled at that stage.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.3","4B.7","4B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; reports a contemporaneous directive and implementation status.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the instructions to President Félix Tshisekedi through his communication to the Council of Ministers.","limitations":["The report documents the directive and enrollment figures but not whether all violations were investigated, punished, or remedied.","The enrollment figure is reported by the CENI, not independently verified in this document."]},{"source_id":"SRC-893cf3bbb191ad95","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported in May 2023 that Tshisekedi's state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri had been extended more than 50 times over two years without genuine public debate; it had transferred civilian administration to military and police authorities, subjected civilians to military courts, restricted rights, and coincided with worsening security, increased civilian attacks, more than 4,000 civilian deaths, and more than two million forced displacements since 2021. Amnesty also reported harassment and imprisonment of journalists, killings of human-rights defenders and political activists, mass pretrial detention, and serious abuses by security forces appointed by Tshisekedi.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the ruler's conduct and institutional conditions during 2023, while some outcomes and the state-of-siege history begin in 2021.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes establishment and continuation of the state of siege to Tshisekedi and attributes appointments of military and police authorities to him.","limitations":["Amnesty International's account is an external human-rights assessment and does not provide the government's full response or a court determination for every allegation.","The casualty and displacement figures cover the period since 2021 rather than 2023 alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0d17151edc0c4193","start_unit":5,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"On 24 March 2023, Tshisekedi reshuffled the government while retaining Prime Minister Sama Lukonde and appointing Jean-Pierre Bemba as Defense Minister, Vital Kamerhe as Economy Minister, Peter Kazadi as Interior, Security and Customary Affairs Minister, and Antipas Mbusa Nyamwisi as Minister of Regional Cooperation; the cabinet also included ministers responsible for justice, finance, planning, infrastructure, health, education, social affairs, and other portfolios.","question_ids":["5B.2","8B.2","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; documents appointments but not subsequent performance.","ruler_attribution":"The source explicitly reports that Tshisekedi carried out the government reshuffle and lists the resulting appointments.","limitations":["The document provides no evidence about the appointees' qualifications, independence, execution, or later replacement.","Cabinet composition alone does not establish effective coordination or policy outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4a646acf88a413eb","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In 2023, five laws were adopted and enacted concerning Indigenous Peoples' rights and natural-resource management, human-rights defenders, reparation for victims of sexual violence and crimes against humanity, trafficking in persons, and penitentiary principles. UNDP-supported recruitment and training of 2,500 magistrates, 34% women, increased the magistrate ratio from 4.4 to 6.9 per 100,000 people, a 56% improvement over 2022; 9,155 people, including 5,414 women, received access to justice. Mobile courts handled 190 ordinary cases and issued 159 judgments, including 121 convictions and 38 acquittals; three verdicts in priority cases produced six convictions for sexual slavery as a crime against humanity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.10","4B.4","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 legislation, staffing, justice access, and case outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes measures undertaken with support from UNDP and the Congolese Government; it does not attribute each action personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["External UNDP support materially contributed to the reported results, so presidential causation is not isolated.","The document reports outputs and selected case outcomes, not nationwide justice quality or durable reduction in abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4a646acf88a413eb","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In North Kivu and Tanganyika during 2023, UNDP and partners trained 75 judicial police officers, including 10 women, in data collection, analysis, and investigation of crimes and human-rights violations; established and equipped a Criminal Analysis Bureau covering both provinces; convened a June 2023 Goma roundtable between judicial police and prosecutors that produced coordination recommendations; and prepared an operational review of the police-inspection department in Kalemie.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 institutional and training activities, with some initiatives begun in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the activities primarily to UNDP, UNPOL, MONUSCO, and Congolese police institutions, aligned with the Congolese National Police action plan.","limitations":["The document does not establish that Tshisekedi personally directed or funded these measures.","Recommendations and a bureau's establishment do not demonstrate effective nationwide implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-25729690842efa0a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Congolese government and education partners validated the third national education-system report (RESEN III), a long-term prospective diagnosis identifying barriers to SDG 4 and priorities for the 2016-2023 education strategy. The process involved about 80 participants, four education ministries, other ministries, civil society, national experts, and an international expert; drafts were reviewed and amended before validation, subject to further amendments.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.2","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The validation occurred in October 2022 and was updated September 2023; it informs the 2023 period but is not itself a 2023 service outcome.","ruler_attribution":"The source credits the government and education partners with initiating and validating the diagnostic process; it does not identify a personal Tshisekedi decision.","limitations":["The document reports planning and diagnostic work, not executed education budgets, implementation, or learning outcomes.","The report's 2016-2023 strategy predates the target year and is not shown here as fully implemented."]},{"source_id":"SRC-20bea8b7127e9493","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Reuters reported that in the Lake Kivu methane auction, the government selected Canadian start-up Alfajiri despite an October 2022 government evaluation finding it lacked the required three years of financial records. A technical report initially scored Alfajiri last at 30.7/100, citing inadequate qualified staff, no feasibility study or timetable, and failure to address public-safety issues; a second version raised its score to 55.75 and placed it first. The minister responsible denied wrongdoing, while Tshisekedi's office declined comment.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.6","7B.9","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reporting and award occurred in 2023, while the cited eligibility and technical reports date from 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The source links the auction to the government and reports Tshisekedi's anti-opacity pledge; it does not show that Tshisekedi personally ordered or benefited from the alleged irregularity.","limitations":["Reuters reported documentary irregularities and allegations but did not establish who ordered the report alteration or the motive.","The source records ministerial and company denials and no final judicial or audit finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-eed13a81f9dec6dd","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A Reuters/TBIJ investigation reported that Alfajiri was admitted to the gas auction despite lacking the three years of financial statements required by regulations; the company's initial technical score of 30.7/100 was later changed to 55.75, placing it first, despite concerns about inadequate staff, absent feasibility study and timetable, public-safety omissions, and insufficient financing for state bonuses and social projects. Sources alleged ministerial intervention, which the minister denied; civil society questioned the selection's transparency.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.6","7B.9","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reported in November 2023 and concerns the 2022-2023 auction process.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the formal auction to the hydrocarbons ministry and reports Tshisekedi's stated transparency commitment; it does not prove personal presidential direction or benefit.","limitations":["This is a corroborating account of the same auction, not an independent presidential finding.","The reported intervention allegations were denied and the document does not report a completed official investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cb6990b08978cc9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"During a December 2023 election rally in Goma, Tshisekedi promised to continue fighting and eliminate M23, blamed Rwanda's Paul Kagame for backing the rebels, praised the army and Wazalendo fighters, and called for UN peacekeepers to leave because he said their protection mission had failed. The article reported that M23 controlled large parts of the region, more than 120 armed groups were active in eastern Congo, and elections would not be held in some conflict-affected areas; the electoral commission had sought government help distributing ballots to insecure areas.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.7","2B.10","3B.3","3B.6","3B.9","4B.1","4B.8","8B.1","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns Tshisekedi's December 2023 campaign rhetoric and the contemporaneous conflict and electoral conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly quotes Tshisekedi's promises, attribution of blame, praise of forces, and position on UN peacekeepers.","limitations":["The article records campaign statements and contextual conditions, not whether the promised military objective was achieved.","The report does not independently establish the factual accuracy of the allegation that Rwanda backed M23."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3136394cedad6e56","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The 2023 Global Report on Food Crises identified the Democratic Republic of the Congo among the five countries containing more than 40% of the global population in acute food insecurity at crisis level or worse in 2022, and among four countries containing more than half of the 35 million people experiencing emergency-level acute hunger. The report identified conflict, economic shocks, and weather extremes as interacting drivers and called for prevention, anticipatory action, shock-responsive safety nets, and greater investment in food systems and child-malnutrition prevention.","question_ids":["6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in 2023 but reports 2022 conditions and global recommendations; it provides baseline/context rather than a direct 2023 presidential action.","ruler_attribution":"No direct action is attributed to Tshisekedi; the DRC appears as a country context in a global assessment.","limitations":["The report does not give a DRC-specific headcount in the cited units or assess Tshisekedi's policies.","The evidence is contextual and cannot establish change during 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains several documents outside the target period or with indirect presidential attribution; those facts are retained only where they materially provide 2023 evidence or a clearly identified baseline/context.","No supplied document provides material evidence for nuclear-risk questions 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.5, 1B.6, 1B.7, or 1B.8, or for several ruler-specific integrity and economic-outcome lenses.","The two gas-auction reports describe the same underlying event and are retained as separate source-specific records because each independently contains materially relevant reporting, while their overlap is noted in limitations."]}
